Other challenges impacting the fresh produce supply chains include logistical and geopolitical issues, economic and labor pressures, and the changing consumer demands, which I have detailed in my nfield report. Therefore, my second recommendation is all stakeholders within the supply chain need to continuously adapt to the ever changing world, which many of the businesses I visited on my travels had started to do. I've taken my learnings from my discussions with stakeholders around the world on what they believe needs to change and how we can make an influence change. And I have built these into a four-step approach. But first, before adopting this approach, we need to change our mindset with both sustainability and resilience in mind. All stakeholders must take shared responsibility to influence and lead change across the supply chain by continuously adapting, ensuring the long-term resilience of the UKâs fresh produce sector.  A Supply Chain Analysis of the Agri-Food Sector in Northern Ghana [...] ###### Agri-food systems are central to sustainable development, linking farmers to consumers through complex supply chains that encompass input supply, production, processing, storage, distribution, and retail. results.title: The challenges of fresh food logistics in Africa
results.content:
### National fresh food logistics challenges

Nationally, the main challenges in fresh food logistics stem from limited infrastructural investment and inadequate Information and Communication Technology (ICT). Long distance transport is often hampered by substandard road, rail, and freight systems. Meanwhile inadequate trade technology, poor demand forecasting, and limited ICT implementation frequently result in ineffective inventory management, logistical issues and further wastage. This is exacerbated by the lack of cold storage facilities.

### International fresh food logistics challenges [...] Modernising the vehicles themselves could also prove beneficial. Equipping farmers with refrigerated storage and vehicles would extend the perishability of fresh produce, as high temperatures are one of the primary causes of spoilage in the region. Cold chain logistics may prove difficult though, given the high cost and inconsistent supply of electricity in some parts of Africa.

### National fresh food logistics challenges [...] FM Agribusiness advisor logo
fresh food logistics header

# The challenges of fresh food logistics in Africa

For most food products, the journey from farm to fork is a complex, multi-step process. The food we eat on a daily basis reaches us through intricate and deeply integrated supply chains, with products moving from producer to consumer via an interconnected network of processors, distributors, and retailers. Food logistics is crucial to overseeing the efficient forward flow of food along this supply chain. It encompasses the packaging, shipping, and delivery of food products downstream, essentially tying the entire chain together.

Sustainable cooling systems and cold chain infrastructure are vital for reducing food waste, enhancing agricultural productivity and incomes, and combating hunger. Each year, Ghana loses or wastes 3.2 million tons of food in the supply chain, costing the country around GHS 762.32 billion (#9). This food loss exacerbates food insecurity, with around 12.9 million people in Ghana affected by moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022 (#10). Developing cold chain infrastructure could significantly reduce post-harvest losses, ensuring that perishable, nutritious crops and fresh produce are stored and transported effectively. This would not only increase food availability and improve nutrition, but also boost incomes for those dependent on agriculture and food production, including the [...] However, the development of Ghanaâs agricultural cold chain faces several challenges, including financial constraints for farmers and agribusinesses, limited access to capital and inadequate infrastructure. The lack of refrigerated transport vehicles and logistical support further hampers progress. To address these challenges, investments in infrastructure, capacity building and financial support are needed. Public-private partnerships and targeted policy interventions will be essential to building a robust and efficient cold chain system, ensuring that Ghana can fully realize the economic and social benefits of sustainable cooling.
